correctness.rationale: For every full-column-rank \(A\), nonstationary residual and mirrored block partition, the source probability aggregates exactly to \(w_j/\sum_kw_k\), and orthogonal projection gives \(d_j=g_j^{\mathsf T}H_j^{-1}g_j\). Principal-submatrix spectral inclusion yields \(a d_j\le w_j\le b d_j\). The Cauchy/bounded-moment argument proves the exact universal coefficient including zero-block and equal-curvature endpoints. The full-rank diagonal four-column family attains equality for every \(\kappa\ge1\); rational example gives decrease ratio \(16/25\). A standalone checker at the actual `verify.py` path passed 1,269 exact-projection and rational-sharpness cases. Finite checks are supportive, not proofs of universal quantifiers.

value.rationale: A published gradient-weighted reflected-block least-squares solver motivates whether its raw-gradient sampling genuinely prioritizes the most effective exact block step. The sharp condition-number ratio and four-column extremizers quantify the precise calibration loss, show arbitrarily severe relative one-step degradation, and distinguish known progress-normalized sampling from the published rule. This sharp algorithmic boundary is neither an arbitrary numerical slice nor merely implementation verification; claims are restricted to one-step squared-residual progress, not downstream speedups.
